What was your first distinctly MGTOW moment?

Here's mine:

When I was 15, I went to a birthday party with my girlfriend, who could drive (17). When I got back around midnight, and went to my room, I noticed that my computer's monitor was black. When I had left I was playing a game called The Dig, which, if I left running would cause my computer to not run a screen saver and also not put my monitor to sleep. So I immediately knew something was wrong. I woke my computer up to find just the operating system was running, and my desktop was strangely bare. I quickly discovered that everything was gone, complete reformat. It didn't take me long to figure out how this had happened.. For the next 2 hours, without leaving my room, I packed up all the stuff I cared about in whatever containers/bags I had.

In the morning I asked my mom and stepdad what they had done, and just as I had suspected, my mom had gotten my stepdad, the family computer wiz, to reformat my computer while I was at the party because she thought I was playing too many video games instead of doing my homework. I told her she also wiped all my homework, particularly all the programs I had been working on for AP Comp Sci. Everything was gone, and she still thought it was justified.

I had already called my girlfriend, she came and picked me up, we got pizza, and she took me to my dad's house, where I lived until going off to college. I will never forget the arrogance my mom displayed as I was walking out the door and she said, "Let me know when you want to come back." To which I replied, "Don't count on it."

Interesting to note: I later dumped this girlfriend because she thought it was ok to bite my lip extremely hard out of spite one evening, I thought she was going to bite it off. I'm glad she didn't...

I can't say I have any moment in particular. However, over this summer I've sort of had a realization that I've been living a MGTOW life. I spend my time going to the gym to get bigger simply for the sake of being the biggest version of myself. I shave my head not to look good but because it's functional and cheap. I spend the rest of my day programming, because I have projects that I REALLY want to make. I ain't got time for women, I gotta finish my work, dammit!

My moment might seem rather conventional, but it was my moment. I grew up in a distinctly christian, conservative, very affluent household. My parents expected me to go to school for finance, or pre-medicine, or business administration. I remember the day when I changed my proposed major during freshman orientation from finance to biology, with a focus on zoology & ecology. I remember the entire way home almost my mother and father grilled me with questions about what I would do to support a family someday (it's sometimes hard as a scientist to even make a living), if I believed in evolution (I'm going to a PhD program in Evolutionary Biology, so the answer to that is obvious), and if I believed in God anymore (I do not). I'll never forget what I said to them: "Frankly, I don't care about any of that. I'm going to be a scientist." They still don't support that decision and they let me know whenever they see me. But, frankly, I don't care. I'm going to be a scientist.
Good for you for standing up to them and for going for what you want.
